tiles.notes:
Tensor-core-style tile: 8x8 PE array runs as systolic matmul with
weight-stationary accumulation, yielding 128 INT8 ops/PE/cycle
(vs 8 ops/PE/cycle for the simple rows*cols*2 model). Used for
large-matrix LLM inference workloads.

blocks.name: pe_int8
blocks.notes:
INT8 PE @ N7 with per-PE register state rolled in. ~20K
transistors per PE (datacenter PEs carry larger weight buffers
than edge SKUs).

blocks.name: pe_matrix
blocks.notes:
Matrix PE is much larger -- systolic cell with 8x-deep
accumulator pipeline + weight registers + input forwarding +
per-PE L1. ~300K transistors per cell.

blocks.name: l1_sram
blocks.notes: Fabric-edge stream storage, per compute tile

blocks.name: noc_routers
blocks.notes: 32-byte flit routers with deep buffers for datacenter NoC

blocks.name: memory_phys
blocks.notes: HBM3 PHY is heavy -- ~200 Mtx per controller, dominates analog area

blocks.name: io_pads
blocks.notes: PCIe Gen5 x16 + power management + sideband

input.name: Stillwater KPU-T768
input.notes:
Datacenter-class KPU SKU for AI inference at scale. 768 heterogeneous
tiles in a 32x24 grid; INT8/BF16 tiles use 16x8 PE arrays while Matrix
tiles use 8x8 systolic blocks (tensor-core-style) for LLM inference.
192 MiB distributed L3 scratchpad. HBM3 64 GB / 1.6 TB/s. TSMC N7
process. 60W default TDP with 30W and 100W profiles; 100W requires
liquid cooling.

Validates the schema's tensor-core-style tile path: Matrix tiles have
8192 INT8 ops/clock at 64 PEs (128 ops/PE/cycle) via systolic
accumulation, which the simple rows*cols*ops_per_pe model would
underestimate by 16x.
